name: find
intro: Read documents. The first argument is the filter, the second picks which fields come back.
notes: `{ age: { $gte: 30 } }` keeps documents whose age is 30 or more.
`{ _id: 0, first_name: 1, ... }` is a projection: 1 includes a field, `_id: 0` drops the default `_id`.
sql: SELECT first_name, last_name, age FROM users WHERE age >= 30;

name: insertOne
intro: Add one document to the collection. No table or column list is declared first.
notes: `insertOne` adds a single document and reports its `_id`.
We supply `_id: 8`; left out, MongoDB generates an ObjectId.
sql: INSERT INTO users (user_id, first_name, last_name, age) VALUES (8, 'John', 'Doe', 30);

name: updateOne
intro: Change one document: the first argument finds it, the second says what to set.
notes: `$set` assigns new values and leaves every other field alone.
`matchedCount` is how many documents the filter found, `modifiedCount` how many actually changed.
sql: UPDATE users SET age = 31 WHERE first_name = 'John' AND last_name = 'Doe';

name: deleteMany
intro: Remove every document that matches the filter.
notes: `deleteMany` removes all matches; `deleteOne` would remove only the first.
An empty filter `{}` matches everything, so read the filter twice.

name: countDocuments
intro: Count the documents in a collection.
notes: `countDocuments({})` counts every document; pass a filter to count only some.

name: $sum
intro: Add up one field across all documents with an aggregation pipeline.
notes: `$group` with `_id: null` puts every document in one group.
`$sum: "$order_amount"` adds the field named after the dollar sign.
sql: SELECT SUM(order_amount) AS total_sales FROM orders;

name: $avg
intro: Average one field across all documents.
notes: `$avg` ignores documents where the field is missing or not a number.
sql: SELECT AVG(age) AS average_age FROM users;

name: $group
intro: One output document per distinct value of a field.
notes: `_id: "$age"` is the group key: one output document per age.
`$sum: 1` counts the documents in each group.
sql: SELECT age, COUNT(*) AS count FROM users GROUP BY age;

name: $lookup + $unwind (inner join)
intro: Attach each user's orders, then split one document per order. Users with no orders disappear.
notes: `$lookup` adds an array `o` of matching orders to each user, empty if none.
`$unwind: "$o"` emits one document per array element and drops empty arrays, which is what makes this an inner join.
sql: SELECT users.first_name, users.last_name, orders.order_id FROM users INNER JOIN orders ON users.user_id = orders.user_id;

name: $lookup + $unwind, preserved (left join)
intro: The same pipeline, but users with no orders are kept.
notes: `preserveNullAndEmptyArrays: true` keeps a user whose array is empty.
There is no NULL: where the user has no order, the `order_id` field is simply absent from the document.
sql: SELECT users.first_name, users.last_name, orders.order_id FROM users LEFT JOIN orders ON users.user_id = orders.user_id;

name: $lookup from the other side (right join)
intro: MongoDB has no RIGHT JOIN. Run the left join from the orders collection instead.
notes: Starting from `orders` and preserving unmatched ones is a right join of users and orders.
Order 107 points at user 99, who does not exist, so its document has no name fields.
sql: SELECT users.first_name, users.last_name, orders.order_id FROM users RIGHT JOIN orders ON users.user_id = orders.user_id;
